nodes.n: World Cup final. 1:30 PM. The hosts have made two hundred and eighty-one. In the dressing room, nobody is talking. Harpreet is eating a banana very slowly, like it's the last one on earth.

nodes.t: Two-eighty-two. It's a lot. It's not too much. We've chased more on worse pitches with worse bowling and much worse food.
{first}. Whatever happens at the top, you're the one I need at the end. Don't try to win it in the first over. Win it in the last.

nodes.n: It goes wrong fast. A run-out in the second over. Then Liam Corrigan, the fastest bowler in the world, the man who bowled at you in the warm-up, takes two wickets in four balls.
Forty for four. Eleventh over. Sixty thousand people in white and red make a sound like a cliff falling. You walk out.
In Kuttanad, it's 7 PM. The bedsheet glows. There are more than a thousand people on the riverbank now, from three villages, and not one of them is talking.
Sameer is at the other end. He hasn't scored for fifteen balls. He walks down the pitch and taps your gloves.

nodes.t: Remember the plan. Bat time. Then runs. Then win.

choice.t: "Bat time. I'll take Corrigan. You take the spinners."
"Let's run them ragged. Ones and twos. Make them tired."

nodes.n: For thirty overs, you don't hit a single boundary that matters. You run. You push into gaps. You turn ones into twos. Sameer runs like a man half his age.
Corrigan comes back for a second spell and you take him on: a pull, a drive, a cut. Three fours in one over. In the stands, a woman in a navy coat over a cream saree stands up and won't sit down.
By the thirtieth over, three fielders have their hands on their knees. Their captain shouts at them. You and Sameer touch gloves after every single run.
Forty-first over. Sameer is caught at deep midwicket for eighty-seven. He stands still for a moment, looking at the sky. Then he walks off, and as he passes you he says only one word.
Two hundred and nine for five. Seventy-three needed from nine overs. The tail is coming. Harpreet is putting his helmet on upside down.

msgs.t: I can see Amma on the TV.
She's praying with her eyes OPEN.

choice.t: Close your eyes for three seconds and see the boat.

nodes.n: Eighth over to go. Sixth over to go. Your score passes ninety. Wickets fall at the other end and you keep the strike like a man guarding a door.
Forty-eighth over. Corrigan is warming up for the last over. You're on ninety-six. India need twelve. One wicket left.

nodes.cliff: Twelve to win. One wicket left. Six balls from the fastest bowler in the world. You're on 96.
